Ref Statement of Work, Equipment Support: Where legacy Bosch, Pelco, or compatible devices are EOL/discontinued and cannot be repaired in kind, will replacement with current-generation equivalents be processed under CLIN 0002 subject to COR approval? ANSWER: Yes, they are subject to COR approval and should be standardized with Avigilon Brand devices (cameras, NVRs and any other Avigilon equipment, accessories needed for the system) 15. Ref Project Documents / System Surveys: Will the Government provide an inventory list (showing model numbers, serial numbers, firmware/software versions, licensing status, server/NVR counts, and warranty status), C-CURE/Victor serial numbers, and as-built drawings/site maps for all sites? ANSWER: The Government will provide any documents available on hand of cameras, NVRs, make models, facility maps. Please note we do not have maps with camera installation locations. In Avigilon System most cameras are labeled with location. There are some cameras which are not and will require working with VA Police to label them properly. 16. Ref Statement of Work, PM Inspections: Is the initial baseline system survey included in the fixed price or billable separately if pre-existing deficiencies are found? Addit

or to all system components, including cameras, servers, NVRs, storage devices, network equipment, power supplies, and other OEM hardware. Certain components may have OEM lead times ranging from several weeks to multiple months depending on manufacturer availability and supply chain conditions. If the eight-hour replacement requirement applies to all components, offerors request that the requirement be modified to account for manufacturer lead times, warranty/RMA timelines, and supply chain delays outside the contractor’s control. ANSWER: This applies to all system components ideally depending on manufacturer’s availability. 22. Software Licensing, Firmware, Updates, and Manufacturer Support SOW Description / Technical Support, Paragraph C: The SOW requires the contractor to support Avigilon licenses, software updates, firmware updates, and the latest validated firmware and software versions on all equipment. Please clarify whether current software licenses, manufacturer support agreements, software assurance, firmware entitlement, and update rights are Government-furnished and active, or whether the contractor is expected to procure and maintain these licenses and support agreements under this contract. The current software licenses, manufacturer support agreements, software assur

manufacturer support agreements, software assurance, firmware entitlement, and update rights are Government-furnished and active. If the contractor is responsible for procuring or renewing software licenses, firmware entitlement, manufacturer support, or subscription-based services, please provide the current license inventory, expiration dates, license quantities, manufacturer support status, and applicable product versions. ANSWER: The contractor is responsible for procuring and renewing software licenses, firmware entitlements, manufacturer support, or subscription-based services. We currently have licenses for cameras per site. Avigilon licensing is complex. I do not have further information to provide. The contractor can have an idea of the licenses amount based on our number of cameras in use. ……. 23. Six-Month 4K Video Retention Requirement Technical Support, Paragraph D: The SOW requires all NVRs to retain a minimum of six (6) months of recorded video at 4K or higher image resolution per camera. Please provide the current number of cameras, recording resolution, frame rate, compression settings, retention settings, storage capacity, storage utilization, and current retention period for each NVR/storage system. About 750 cameras connected. There may be another 200 not connected

Definitions "Breach" is defined as the loss of control, compromise, unauthorized disclosure, unauthorized acquisition, or any similar occurrence where- (a) A person other than an authorized user accesses or potentially accesses Personally Identifiable Information (PII); or (b) An authorized user accesses or potentially accesses PII for an unauthorized purpose. "Information" is defined as any communication or representation of knowledge such as facts, data, or opinions in any medium or form, including textual, numerical, graphic, cartographic, narrative, electronic, or audiovisual forms (see Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular No. A-130, Managing Federal Information as a Strategic Resource). "Information System" is defined as a discrete set of information resources organized for the collection, processing, maintenance, use, sharing, dissemination, or disposition of information (44 U.S.C. 3502). "Personally Identifiable Information" is defined as information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity, either alone or when combined with other information that is linked or linkable to a specific individual (see OMB Circular No. A-130, Managing Federal Information as a Strategic Resource). This deliverable would traditionally include the clinical scenarios, scenes, visual descriptions and placeholders, plans for interactions, voiceover script, on-screen text, planned media treatments, and developer notes? Should this deliverable be called a storyboard, detailed design document, production script, scenario specification, or another Government-defined term, and is it separate from the project plan referenced in Milestone 1? Project Plan A project management document outlining the key phases, tasks, dependencies, timeline, and resource allocations required to develop and deliver the Agitation 360 application. This document will serve as the governing schedule and coordination tool for the Contractor and GRECC team throughout the period of performance. 2. Design Document / Scenario Specific

erience. The GRECC would like to work with the designer to develop three web-based scenarios based on caregiver interviews. (IT) SYSTEM In accordance with DON CIO Memorandum (IT LEVEL DESIGNATION ON DD FORM 2875 SYSTEM AUTHORIZATION ACCESS REQUEST) 08 September 2020, contractor employees who require access to Department of the Navy (DoN) or DoD networks are categorized as Privileged, Enhanced, or Authorized users. All user level accesses may include positions which require access to Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). CUI includes sensitive information protected under the Privacy Act, to include Protected Health Information (PHI). IT System levels are determined by the requiring activity's Command Information System Security Manager (ISSM)/Information Assurance Manager (IAM). Contractor employees requiring privileged access, (when specified by the terms of the contract) require a Tier 5 (T5) or T5R equivalent investigation, which is a higher level investigation than the Tier 3 (T3) and T3R described below. Due to the privileged system access, an investigation suitable for High Risk national security positions is required. Individuals who have access to system control, monitoring, or administration functions (e.g. system administrator, database administrator) require training and certification to Information Assurance (IA) Technical Level 1, and must be trained and certified on the Operating Sys

iring activity's Command Information System Security Manager (ISSM)/Information Assurance Manager (IAM). Due to the privileged system access, an investigation suitable for High Risk national security positions is required. Individuals who have access to system control, monitoring, or administration functions (e.g. system administrator, database administrator) require training and certification to Information Assurance (IA) Technical Level 1, and must be trained and certified on the Operating System or Computing Environment they are required to maintain. Contractors requiring Enhanced access, (when specified by the terms of the contract) require a T3, T3R, or equivalent investigation, which is a higher level investigation than the Tier 1 (T1) described below. White Paper Review and Selection Process (First Step) : Evaluation of white papers will be conducted by a peer or scientific review process, using the criteria described above (or as outlined at the Individual Solicitation level). ly and technically sound approach and/or not relevant to mission needs Under the Open ARA, White Papers may be submitted at any time; however, the submissions will be evaluated within 3 months after White Paper submission at minimum. Proposal Review and Selection Process (Second Step) : Proposals requested after white papers will also be reviewed against the criteria described above. Based on the peer or scientific review process, proposals will be categorized as: Highly Recommended: Well-conceived scientifically and technically sound proposal pertinent to accomplish goals and objectives. Proposals are recommended for acceptance (subject to availability of funds) and normally are displaced only by other Highly Recommended proposals. Selectable: Scientifically or technically sound proposals that may need additional development. Proposals are recommended for acceptance if sufficient funding is available, but at a lower priority than Highly Recommended proposals. To ensure a diversity of approaches, a Selectable proposal may be prioritized over a Highly Recommended proposal if the Selectable proposal presents a unique approach unlike any of the Highly Recommended proposals. Contractor Employees Requiring Access to Government Information Systems: Contractor shall have access to Government-controlled information systems during performance of work under this contract. All contractor employees and associated subcontractors who require access to a Government information system shall be registered in the ATCTS (Army Training Certification Tracking System) at commencement of support services and must successfully complete the DoD Information Assurance Awareness prior to access to the information systems. Training shall be required annually after the initial training. Completion certificates shall be submitted to the COR within fifteen (15) calendar days from date of commencing performance under this contract. 1.6.8.1.11. OPSEC Training: Per AR 530-1, Operations Security, new Contractor employees must complete Level I OPSEC training within 30 days of reporting for duty. All contract employees must complete annual OPSEC Awareness Training.

Safety Data Sheets will be provided to sites as appropriate for supplies containing hazardous chemicals. ture stability up to 52 hours. Post-vasectomy testing kits with unlimited retesting until absence of sperm is resulted in subsequent semen specimens. CSOs are subject to the limitations outlined in the General Services Acquisition Manual (GSAM) Part 571 and the associated CSO Guide. CSO procedures can be utilized to competitively procure innovative commercial products and commercial services to include innovative technologies and solutions using the commercial solutions opening. The purpose of the proposed requirement is to provide hands-on cross connection control trainings for tribal utility and IHS staff in the lower 48 States and Alaska. The successful vendor(s) will be able to provide off-the-shelf and customized trainings and certifications (or certification facilitation). Purchase Order No. 75H70726Q00095 Project Title Cross Connection Control Training - OEHE Page 5 of 17 5.1.2 Instructor Qualifications Instructor experience shall be integral to the Vendor’s selection. Instructor qualifications, as demonstrated through the proposal CV/resumes, shall include: •A minimum of five (5) years’ experience in water operations serving communities ranging from 15 to 2500 connections. While not required. Instructors with operator certification levels 2 or higher in water distribution, water treatment, wastewater collections, wastewater treatment, and/or utility management is a plus. •A minimum of five (5) years’ experience in providing cross control training and support to tribal utility departments or small rural communities. Tribal experience is preferable. •Evidence of adult education competencies (e.g., adult education training courses attended, experience teaching adults

luding the exercise of any options under this clause, shall not exceed five years and 6 months. Purchase Order No. 75H70726Q00095 Project Title Cross Connection Control Training - OEHE Page 12 of 17 This contract incorporates the following Health and Human Services Acquisition Regulation (HHSAR) clauses by reference, with the same force and effect as if they were provided in full text. As used in this clause— Payment request means a bill, voucher, invoice, or request for contract financing payment with associated supporting documentation. The payment request must comply with the requirements identified in FAR 32.905(b), “Content of Invoices” and the applicable Payment clause included in this contract. (b) Except as provided in paragraph (c) of this clause, the Contractor shall submit payment requests elec

g other than IPP only when the Contracting Officer authorizes alternate procedures in writing in accordance with HHS procedures. ORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) Logistics Fundamentals and Supply Chain Management Training 1.0 BACKGROUND The Marine Corps Logistics Command (MARCORLOGCOM) mission is to provide worldwide, integrated logistics, supply chain, and distribution management; depot-level maintenance management; and strategic pre-positioning capability in support of the operating forces and other supported units. This support maximizes organizational readiness and sustainability, while driving enterprise and program-level Total Life Cycle Management. MARCORLOGCOM is comprised of two subordinate commands: • Marine Depot Maintenance Command (MDMC) • Blount Island Command Additionally, it consists of five dedicated centers: • Marine Forces Storage Center • Weapons System Management Center • Logistics Services Management Center • Quality Management Center • Maintenance Management Center Each of these organizations has a direct, critical role in supporting and executing the Command’s primary mission. MARCORLOGCOM’s Workforce-21 initiative is a proactive workforce development strategy designed to sustain a highly capable, agile workforce prepared to operate within a dynamic and digitally connected logistics environment. To support the professional growth of its personnel within the Logistics

gitally connected logistics environment. To support the professional growth of its personnel within the Logistics Community of Interest (COI) occupational series (0346, 2010, 2003, 2005), MARCORLOGCOM requires a comprehensive training program. This program will enable up to twenty-five (25) individuals to obtain professional certificates across two structured tracks: a Logistics Fundamentals Certificate Program (Entry-Level) and a subsequent Supply Chain Management Certificate Program (Journeyman-Level). 2.0 SCOPE OF REQUIREMENT The Contractor shall provide all qualified personnel, labor, instructional materials, coordination, and travel necessary to deliver a one-time facilitation of six (6) professional training courses for a single cohort of up to twenty-five (25) participants. The program is structured as follows: • Four (4) Logistics Fundamentals (Entry-Level) Courses • Two (2) Supply Chain Management (Journeyman-Level) Courses 2.1 Delivery Structure and Duration • Course Duration: To maximize knowledge retention and allow students to apply concepts in real-time, each class shall be one (1) month in duration. We serve the uniformed services and the Nation as an outstanding academic health sciences center with a worldwide perspective for education, research, service, and consultation; we are unique in relating these activities to military medicine, disaster medicine, and military medical readiness. USU is located in Bethesda, MD on the grounds of the Naval Support Activity Bethesda. The mission of the USU is to provide the highest quality education programs in the health sciences to those selected individuals who demonstrate dedication to a health profession career in the Uniformed Services. subcontracting_consortium.text: ip Award of the Phase 1 OT is the beginning of our collaborative partnership, not the end of the acquisition. Upon award, the selected Design-Builder will immediately integrate with the USACE and Air Force team to begin the Phase 1 design and pre-construction phase. This is a transparent, hands-on process. Key Activities in Phase 1: Jointly Develop the Design: You will participate in regular "Over-the-Shoulder" design reviews to advance the facility design from concept to a mature, buildable solution (~65% completion). Build the "Open Book" Cost Model: You will be required to transparently build the construction cost estimate, sharing actual subcontractor quotes and material pricing with the Government team. Manage Risk Together: You will co-manage a Joint Risk Register with USACE, working together to identify, price, and mitigate project risks before they become problems. Negotiate the Final Price: At the end of Phase 1, we will use the transparent Open Book model and our IGE to negotiate a fair and reasonable Firm-Fixed-Price for the Phase 2 construction work. Our goal in Phase 1 is to work as a single, unified team to de-risk the project and establish a credible, data-driven price for construction. This is a transparent, hands-on process.</a:t></a:r></a:p><a:p><a:pPr marL="0" indent="0"><a:buNone/></a:pPr><a:r><a:rPr lang="en-US" sz="1550" b="1"/><a:t>Key Activities in Phase 1:</a:t></a:r></a:p><a:p><a:r><a:rPr lang="en-US" sz="1550"/><a:t>Jointly Develop the Design: You will participate in regular "Over-the-Shoulder" design reviews to advance the facility design from concept to a mature, buildable solution (~65% completion).</a:t></a:r></a:p><a:p><a:r><a:rPr lang="en-US" sz="1550"/><a:t>Build the "Open Book" Cost Model: You will be required to transparently build the construction cost estimate, sharing actual subcontractor quotes and material pricing with the Government team.</a:t></a:r></a:p><a:p><a:r><a:rPr lang="en-US" sz="1550"/><a:t>Manage Risk Together: You will co-manage a Joint Risk Register with USACE, working </a:t></a:r><a:br><a:rPr lang="en-US" sz="1550"/></a:br><a:r><a:rPr lang="en-US" sz="1550"/><a:t>together to identify, price, and mitigate project risks before they become problems.</a:t></a:r></a:p><a:p><a:r><a:rPr lang="en-US" sz="1550"/><a:t>Negotiate the Final Price: At the end of Phase 1, we will use the transparent Open </a:t></a:r><a:br><a:rPr lang="en-US" sz="1550"/></a:br><a:r><a:rPr lang="en-US" sz="1550"/><a:t>Book model and our IGE

rice. Beyond Firm Fixed Price and Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP), is USACE considering other commercial pricing models for future OTA Progressive Design Build procurements, such as Cost Plus with a negotiated fee or Construction Manager at Risk style pricing where the contractor is compensated on a fee percentage basis? 12 For now, we will always post on SAM.gov; we expect other possibilities in the next few years but unsure on when exactly. How does USACE envision future OTA opportunities being announced? Will they generally be publicly advertised through SAM.gov, or should industry expect some opportunities to be released through consortiums, commercial solutions openings, or other invitation based processes? 13 Currently, USACE is using OTs for a wide range of projects. OTs are best suited for complex projects which rely on innovative technical solutions. They are also suited for projects which require significant involvement between the contractor and the end-user. This will not be limited to certain types of projects. What types of projects does USACE anticipate being the best candidates for OTA procurement? Will this be limited to highly innovative projects like cyber, AI, and Industrialized Construction, or do you foresee broader application to military construction?
